subject: Request: enterprise SLA addendum & order-form language (uptime/latency evidence)
messages:
From: Ellen Price <ellen.price@clearpathmedical.com>
To: naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.example>, procurement@clearpathmedical.com
Cc: Tom Liu <tom.liu@healthtechcounsel.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Custom SLA addendum request — regulatory uptime/evidence

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team is excited about Redwood. Procurement surfaced a few non-standard requirements that we need to lock before we can route to signature under ClearPath's enterprise MSA. High-level asks:

- A written SLA addendum (MSA attachment / SOW exhibit) that commits to 99.95% monthly availability for our production endpoints serving clinical workloads.
- Latency SLO: P95 <= 150ms for text-generation endpoints at steady-state (typical batch size <=16).
- Evidence pack we can produce to our security/compliance team: monitoring dashboard screenshots, 30-day aggregated uptime reports, incident runbook examples, and SOC-2 audit pointers.
- Order form language that explicitly ties the addendum to the order form (so the availability exhibit is bound to the order) and clear credit calculations for outages.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide a tailored addendum and the evidence pack? If so, please share a draft and an estimated timeline. We'd like to keep this in the procurement window for this quarter.

Attached: ClearPath_SLA_Expectations.pdf (PDF) — internal summary from procurement.

Thanks,
Ellen Price
Sr. Director, Procurement
ClearPath Medical
ellen.price@clearpathmedical.com

Thanks Naomi — I reviewed ClearPath's expectations and drafted redlines. High-level thoughts:

- 99.95% monthly availability is aggressive but doable for hosted endpoints with our Dedicated pools and correct routing; we should qualify with an exclusion for scheduled maintenance windows and force-majors.
- Latency P95 <=150ms: we need to be explicit about payload size, model family and concurrency. Suggest language: "P95 token/response latency for typical payloads (<= 2,048 tokens and batch size <=16) measured at the Redwood edge to the nearest customer-facing region." This keeps it testable.
- Evidence pack: we can supply a 30-day availability export from internal SLO tooling, Grafana dashboard links (customer-safe screenshots), and a redacted incident runbook template. We cannot share raw logs or customer data — must be redacted.
- Credits calc: propose simple pro-rata monthly credit with a floor:
  - Availability >= 99.95%: no credit
  - 99.90% - 99.95%: 5% credit on monthly service charges
  - 99.00% - 99.89%: 15% credit
  - < 99.00%: 30% credit
  (This is negotiable; legal may push for different bands.)

I've attached a redlined addendum and an order-form snippet in msas-exhibit-template-redline.docx. Specific asks for Karthik: can you confirm we have monitoring exports for the last 30 days and whether we can produce a P95 latency report by model family? If yes, we should produce a sample report to include with v1.

If folks are OK, I'll clean the doc and we can send to Ellen and Tom by EOD Thu (8/5).

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Enterprise Contracts
Redwood Inference
